messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps

Hi Alex --

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I'll update.

Key pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable token costs and tail-latency on peak inference traffic (affects user search and real-time triage).
- Data isolation and audit requirements for PHI-adjacent workloads (SOC 2 + customer KMS controls).
- Need for predictable throughput for real-time product features (no noisy neighbor impact).

Primary goals we discussed:
- Reserve dedicated GPU capacity to guarantee baseline throughput for your real-time features.
- Isolate inference workloads in a customer-dedicated VPC with KMS-managed keys and audit logs.
- Achieve p99 latency targets under SLA while keeping unit cost optimized via batching and KV caching.

Redwood recommendation (initial):
- Dedicated capacity: 8x A100 80GB (reserved) as baseline.
  - Baseline pool: 4 GPUs always allocated (handles steady traffic).
  - Burst/autoscale: up to 8 GPUs during peak (policy-based, 15-30 minute warm-up depending on model & shard).
- Isolation: Private VPC peering + customer-managed KMS, SOC 2 audit logs enabled for all inference requests.
- Performance targets: SLA 99.95% uptime for the Dedicated runtime; p99 token generation latency < 120ms for the primary low-latency model (subject to sequence-length constraints).
- Cost levers: quantization profile for non-critical models, prefix caching for hot prompts, and continuous batching policies to reduce per-token cost.

Operational timeline (estimate):
- SOW & pricing confirmed: 1 week after this thread (pending procurement PO).
- Provisioning & network setup (VPC, KMS, peering): ~2 weeks from PO sign-off.
- Load-testing & acceptance window: 1 week (we'll run scaling tests with your sample workloads).

Attachments: I'm attaching the draft SOW (CloverHealth_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_v1.pdf) with the capacity breakdown and a short checklist for procurement.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the procurement contact and expected PO timeline? (I recall Maya Singh is the procurement lead -- looping her when ready.)
2) Would you like a technical deep-dive for your infra team next week? Dylan can lead the session and cover peering, KMS integration, and observability.
3) Are there any additional compliance docs we should include before the SOW (e.g., specific encryption attestations)?

Proposed times for tech deep-dive:
- Thu Nov 19, 10:00-11:00 PT
- Fri Nov 20, 09:00-10:00 PT

Thanks -- looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

- The 8x A100 recommendation sounds right for peak headroom, but can you share a pricing delta between the baseline (4 GPU reserved) and the full 8 GPU reserved configuration? We need numbers for both CapEx/OpEx comparisons.
- Procurement: I've looped in Maya (cc). Maya -- we typically need an itemized SOW and a vendor W9 + master services agreement before issuing a PO. Can Redwood provide the W9 and a redline-friendly MSA?

Also, please include a short runbook for incident escalation and the expected response times for P1/P2 once the Dedicated environment is live.

Notes: pricing above is indicative pending final model/sequence length profile and your acceptance testing results. We can provide a line-item export for procurement.
